cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Bring Back Everything
cards.instruction: Return early details in altered forms until the scene feels like it has been building toward one unavoidable consequence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's use what I taught you. You said 'nothing can go wrong' before balancing the key on the teacup.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It fell into the cup. I dried it with the invitation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're nearly doing it my way. And now the invitation has dissolved around the key to the wedding hall.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can still prise it off.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Your 'nothing' has become both the lock and the address we can't read.

mechanism: A corrects its former event pupil by bringing back tea, invitation and hall key as damaged access information that forces an embarrassing call for directions.
confusable: Not disconnected callbacks: the key-in-tea and invitation used as towel create the specific unreadable-address consequence.
comparison: Useful key without address versus spare chair displaced until teacher loses own seat.
